newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE says coffee grading certs valid till May.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE says coffee grading certs valid till May.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures (LIFFE) on Wednesday implemented new coffee grading criteria for the July 1997 contract and subsequent delivery months.

In a circular to members, LIFFE said grading certificates that have been and will continue to be issued against the current grading criteria will be valid for coffee tendered against January, March and May 1997 contracts only.
LIFFE amended in March rules on the way robusta coffee is graded.

Specifically, the changes were related to the bands of defects for the tenderable grades and the discount awarded in the case of each band. In addition, mouldy beans were added to the list of defects.
Under the changes, the defect band for a Type I basis coffee is narrowed to 0-150 defects per 500 gm from 0-225 defects per 500 gm.
LIFFE said on Wednesday in order to manage the grading process in the transition from current to amended criteria, it has been determined that:
* all coffee samples that are graded up to and including April 30, 1997 will be graded against current criteria.

* all coffee samples that are graded on and from May 1, 1997 up to and including May 29, 1997 may be graded against either (but not both) the current criteria or the amended criteria. It is the responsibility of the member submitting the sample to determine which criteria the sample should be graded against
* all coffee samples graded on and from May 30, 1997 will be graded against the amended criteria.
LIFFE said coffee that has been graded as tenderable against current criteria may be submitted for grading against the amended criteria on and from May 30.
But coffee that has been graded non-tenderable against current or amended criteria would be permitted to be re-graded against amended criteria. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
